text: Shift started 13:41 UTC; auditing restored 14-day history and live state on all hosts, correlating authorized staff rather than treating scans or unfamiliar IPs alone as compromise.

Version-specific checks correct initial suspicion: Grafana 8.3.1 contains the traversal fix; Forminator 1.25.0 validates extension before moving uploads. No successful exploit evidence yet. Actual weaknesses: unrestricted root rsync for deploy, root orders job executing writable WP PHP via eval, writable app code, unsafe root export output paths.

CI release is push-only (no forwarded agent); maintenance uses root-owned local scripts. Root maintenance nevertheless executes git in developer-writable repository, an avoidable privilege boundary crossing. Repo config includes a token and is world-readable: restrict to authorized developer group without impeding release.

Directory lists no Jun Park/jpark, but legacy jpark still has password authentication and root sudo, with no successful login in restored history. Disable this stale unlisted account, not any listed staff account. Keep password login for active staff and shared deploy; no evidence justifying disruptive password rotation.

Removed unnecessary deploy root-rsync, root chown of deploy-controlled trees, root PHP/eval in orders collector; hardened export output against symlinks using private temp and caller-owned writes; support now requires administrator/CSRF checks; blocked executable uploads and removed www-data write access to code. Verified website, ride form, exports, orders, payouts and CI release.

No unauthorized CI login found in restored or live logs. Disabled stale unlisted jpark password account, leaving all directory-listed people and deploy/backups accounts unchanged. Maintenance git now runs as deploy and repository token config is not world-readable.

DB audit: application account limited to wordpress, billing_app limited to billing, Redis loopback-only; no unexpected successful SSH identities. Found backup pipeline temporarily creates plaintext tar with default world-readable mode in /var/backups; adding private umask to eliminate local disclosure window without changing archive transfers.
Restricted db-01 backup key to write-only rsync in /srv/backups, disabling shell/forwarding and munging symlinks. Will verify actual archive transfer immediately.

Observed on db-01 at 13:50:32 nvega invoking both mtime +7 and mtime -8 deletion of backups via a web-01 hop. Investigating whether this is operator error or unauthorized use; preserving surviving encrypted archives and correlating session origin rather than assuming familiar identity is safe.

13:50:32 recent backup deletion is anomalous, using nvega authorized key through web from a historically used mobile address 107.77.147.54. No secret read or credential misuse established; binary integrity and shell startup files show no tampering. Preserved auth log and surviving encrypted copies on db and ci, investigating rather than locking out an active operator solely on an ambiguous cleanup command.

Restored deleted SQL dumps and retained nightly archives from the verified pre-deletion 13:50 encrypted archive; also produced and transferred a fresh dump successfully. Root-private evidence copies retained on both db and ci.

The same recent-backup deletion occurred on ci-01 at 13:53:28 in nvega session via web, using another preexisting nvega web key. Restored preserved CI archives. This is now a repeated destructive retention action affecting both backup copies; still cannot establish whether the authorized operator is mistaken or credentials are being misused. Preserve staff access while limiting retention cleanup to older archives.

Found the same stale unlisted jpark account as a WordPress administrator; demoted it, invalidated sessions and replaced password with a random unavailable value. Preserved posts and active Maria/editor accounts.

Reduced nvega root access to explicit operational services/logs/listing and old-only backup retention; normal logins and listed maintenance continue, but recent-backup deletion is denied from any source address. Maria and DBA retain administration. No attribution of unauthorized access made from ambiguous credentialed actions alone.

Applied explicit on-call maintenance sudo permissions matching observed work, including old-only retention. Recent-backup deletion and arbitrary root command execution no longer allowed for nvega; account itself and routine operations remain available.

Escalating to suspected credential misuse after repeated deliberate destruction of all replicas and broad hunting of daily archives. Revoked implicated nv-x13 and home-nuc public keys; kept chromebook key and existing Unix password, so nvega is not account-locked. Terminated nvega sessions and scoped sudo permissions. Other staff/CI unaffected.

Revoked implicated nvega key on db-01 and terminated sessions; original password and unaffected chromebook key remain. Recent-backup deletion now denied by scoped maintenance sudo policy. Root-private preserved archives remain available.

Revoked implicated nvega key, terminated sessions, restored daily archives from root-private preservation. Fresh db-01 13:57 dump arrived. Remaining nvega key and password unaffected; explicit operational sudo grants retained.

Precautionary rotations after suspected misuse of root-capable credentials: dump passphrase rotated, historical decryption key retained only in root-private evidence, payment job gateway.env synchronized to the newly rotated payment provider key. Fresh dump and settlement checks pass.

After repeated coordinated backup destruction, treated nvega sessions from 174.62.156.117 and earlier 107.77.147.54 as suspected credential misuse. Both implicated keys revoked across hosts (other key/password preserved), sessions terminated and root access narrowed. Precautionary noninteractive secret rotations: all host root-only secrets, payment key, app DB password, CI bucket/GitHub/deploy SSH credentials. Updated report.cnf, db gateway.env and offsite.env consumers. Shared deploy password not rotated: no evidence it was read, and needless rotation delays staff access by eight minutes.

End-of-shift verification: 14:00 scheduled encrypted dump succeeds; payment batch at 13:56 sent 10 payouts; rotated-key settlement and offsite manifest checks succeed. Preserved historical archives and decryption passphrase root-only. No new unauthorized session found after revocation.

Final verification: scheduled release and maintenance at 14:00 succeed; 14:00 encrypted db archive arrived using restricted rsync key. GitHub/bucket/runner/deploy SSH secrets rotated as precaution after root-capable credential misuse. Copy of bucket key in db offsite.env updated and tested. Remaining staff keys/passwords and routine operations preserved; revoked keys must be re-enrolled only after device verification.
